events.content:
Done. All four transition patterns are wired up, and the build, typecheck, and rendered output all verify clean.

## What changed

**`app/ProductGrid.tsx`** — thumbnail wrapped in `<ViewTransition name={`product-image-${slug}`} share="morph" default="none">`; links tagged `transitionTypes={['nav-forward']}`.

**`app/product/[slug]/page.tsx`** — hero wrapped in the matching named `ViewTransition` (same name → React pairs them and animates position/size). Back link tagged `nav-back`. Suspense fallback/content got `exit="slide-down"` / `enter="slide-up"`.

**`app/page.tsx`** — same Suspense pair around the grid skeleton/grid.

Both pages wrap their content in a directional `ViewTransition` keyed on transition type. Per the docs, this wrapper has to live in each `page.tsx`, not the layout — layouts persist across navigation so enter/exit never fire there.

**`app/globals.css`** — the morph (400ms + mid-flight blur), slide-up/down reveals, directional slides, plus `::view-transition { pointer-events: none }` so clicks during an animation aren't swallowed.

**`react-canary.d.ts`** (new) — `ViewTransition`'s types live in `@types/react/canary.d.ts`, which isn't loaded by default; a one-line triple-slash reference pulls them in project-wide.

## Two details worth knowing

**The hero sits outside the Suspense boundary deliberately.** A morph pair only forms when the destination renders in the same commit as the navigation. If you later add a `loading.tsx` or move the hero inside the boundary, the destination suspends into a fallback first, no pair forms, and the image degrades to a plain enter animation.

**`default="none"` requires the explicit `share="morph"`.** With `default="none"` and no `share`, the pair silently stops morphing. `default="none"` is what stops every named image from crossfading on unrelated transitions.

## Reduced motion

I went with the docs' refined option rather than the blunt `animation-duration: 0s` on everything: positional movement and blur are stripped, but a 150ms opacity crossfade is kept — an instant swap would discard the "same object" signal the morph exists to convey, and opacity changes don't trigger motion sensitivity. The `!important` flags are necessary because the named/classed selectors outrank `*`. I also disabled the pre-existing `pulse` skeleton animation, since that's motion too and was previously unguarded.

## Verification

`tsc --noEmit` clean; `next build` compiled and prerendered all 3 routes. The prerender is itself meaningful evidence — if `ViewTransition` had resolved to `undefined` (the root `react` is 19.1.0, which lacks it; Next aliases its vendored canary), prerendering `/` would have thrown on an invalid element type. I confirmed against the running server that every transition prop reaches the RSC payload with matching pair names (`product-image-cotton-hoodie` on both sides), and that the minifier passed the `::view-transition-*` pseudo-elements and `!important` overrides through intact.

Two things I did not do: I skipped the docs' header-anchoring step, as this app has no persistent header to anchor — adding one would be inventing UI. And I left the same-route crossfade pattern out, since there's no same-route content switching here (no tabs or filters). I also left one pre-existing quirk alone: the detail page's root is a plain `<div>` rather than `<main>`, so it doesn't get the max-width and padding the grid has. The morph interpolates real rects so it works correctly regardless, but the hero spans the full viewport width, making the size change more dramatic than it would be otherwise. Wrapping it in `<main>` would tighten that up if you want it — say the word.

I verified the transition wiring structurally, not visually; the actual animation feel is worth a look in a browser (`npm run dev`), since Safari handles some of these differently.
